sermuncŭlus , i, m. dim. sermo.
I. (Acc. to sermo, I. B. 3.) Common talk, tittletattle, report, rumor (rare but class.): “urbani sermunculi,” Cic. Deiot. 12, 33 : “sermunculis fabellisque duci,” Plin. Ep. 5, 8, 4 : “sermunculum omnem aut restinxerit aut sedarit,” Cic. Att. 13, 10, 3 : “non deterreor sermunculis istorum,” Plin. Ep. 7, 17, 14 .—
II. A little discourse (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 32, 1.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
